title: Explain principles of human resources management and practices in agriculture

lessons.title: What human resources management is
lessons.html:
People are the farm's most important resource

Human resources management (HRM) is about how a business finds, employs, trains, pays, looks after and works with its people. On a farm, crops and animals need care every day, so the skills and attitude of workers make a big difference to yields, animal health and safety.

Main HR activities

ActivityWhat it means on a farm
PlanningWorking out how many workers are needed, with which skills, in each season, such as extra pickers at harvest
Recruitment and selectionFinding and choosing the right people fairly
Contracts and inductionWritten contract; showing new workers the farm, the rules, safety and their job
Training and developmentBuilding skills, such as tractor driving, spraying, first aid, pruning
Pay and benefitsPaying at least the legal minimum wage, on time, with a payslip
PerformanceSetting standards, giving feedback, recognising good work
Discipline and grievancesFair procedures when rules are broken or when a worker has a complaint
Health, safety and wellbeingSafe work, protective clothing, clean toilets and water, housing where provided
RecordsAttendance, leave, pay, training and contracts

Permanent and seasonal workers

Farms often employ permanent workers all year and seasonal or temporary workers at busy times. Both groups have rights under labour law. Seasonal workers also need induction, safety training and a written record of their terms.

Why good HR practice pays

  • Workers who are treated fairly stay longer, so skills are not lost.
  • Trained workers make fewer mistakes and have fewer accidents.
  • Fair, clear rules reduce conflict and disputes.
  • Buyers and export markets often audit labour practices on farms.

lessons.title: Labour law and fair practice
lessons.html:
The main labour laws

Farm workers in South Africa are protected by the same main labour laws as other workers. You should know their names and what they cover in general.

  • Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997 – working hours, overtime, rest, leave, notice, payslips. A sectoral determination adds specific rules for farm workers.
  • National Minimum Wage Act 9 of 2018 – the lowest wage that may be paid. The amount is updated, so always check the current figure.
  • Labour Relations Act 66 of 1995 – right to join a trade union, fair dismissal, the CCMA for disputes.
  • Employment Equity Act 55 of 1998 – no unfair discrimination on grounds such as race, gender, disability, religion or HIV status.
  • Skills Development Act 97 of 1998 – training and learnerships; AgriSETA supports agriculture.
  • Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 – a safe workplace.
  • Unemployment Insurance Act 63 of 2001 – UIF registration and contributions.
  • Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993 – compensation if a worker is injured at work.

Principles of fair HR practice

  1. Fairness and consistency – the same rules for everyone.
  2. Transparency – workers know the rules, their pay and how decisions are made.
  3. Respect and dignity – no abuse, shouting or harassment.
  4. Communication – regular meetings, worker committees, listening to concerns.
  5. Fair procedure – before discipline, a worker hears the complaint and can give their side.
  6. Development – opportunities to learn and move up.

Example

A worker on a citrus farm arrives late several times. The supervisor talks to him privately, hears that the farm transport is unreliable, and reports this. The transport is fixed. If the late-coming continues for other reasons, the farm follows its written disciplinary code: first a verbal warning, then a written warning, keeping records at each step.

Key points

  • HRM covers planning, hiring, training, pay, performance, discipline, wellbeing and records.
  • Permanent and seasonal workers both have rights under labour law.
  • Know the main laws: BCEA, National Minimum Wage Act, LRA, EEA, SDA, OHS Act, UIF and COIDA.
  • Fair HR is consistent, transparent, respectful and follows fair procedure.
  • Good HR keeps skilled workers, reduces accidents and satisfies buyers.
